questions.q: Some chart types in the picker are greyed out for a report that has only one grouping. Which types are most likely unavailable?
options: Stacked bar and column charts, which need a second grouping
questions.explain: Stacked and grouped charts split each bar by a second grouping, so they are unavailable when the report has only one.

questions.q: Which chart type best answers 'how has monthly revenue changed over the past year'?
options: Line (or a vertical column chart grouped by month)
questions.explain: Trends over time are best shown with a line, or columns by month, after grouping a date field at month granularity.

questions.q: In the Lightning report and dashboard toolkit, what visual is used where Salesforce Classic offered a pie chart?
questions.explain: Lightning uses donut charts for parts-of-a-whole visuals; use them only with a small number of slices.

questions.q: You need to show a single number, such as pipeline this quarter, prominently against a target. Which options fit best?
options: A metric or gauge dashboard component
questions.explain: Metric (one big number) and Gauge (a number against a range or target) are dashboard components designed for this.

questions.q: Which is a genuine limit of native Salesforce report charts, per this lesson?
options: They cannot show values on the chart
They cannot be used on dashboards
They only work in Salesforce Classic
The set of chart types is fixed, with no maps, heat maps, or custom visuals
questions.explain: Native charts are a small, fixed toolkit with modest styling, which is why CRM Analytics and Tableau exist for richer visuals.
